Ansarul Hoque ------ Plaintiff
vs.
Agrani Bank ------ Defendant"
full_judgment: 7. In the instant case both the High Court Division and the District Court are empowered under Order 37 of the CPC to dispose of suits on negotiable instruments through the summary procedure and we find no limitation on the pecuniary jurisdiction of the District Court in such a matter. The only restriction on the District Court's Jurisdiction is the limit imposed by law limiting the pecuniary jurisdiction for disposal of appeals only. The plaintiff can present his claim in the ordinary court for disposal of his suit and may also choose the court empowered under Order XXXVII of the CPC. But in view of section 15 of the CPC he cannot compel the court of the higher jurisdiction to dispose of his suits. The higher court may entertain the suit and try it or may in the alternative refuse to entertain it directing the plaintiff to present the plaint before the court of the lower jurisdiction in obedience to the provision of section 15 of the CPC. In the present case we do not find lack of jurisdiction for the District Court to dispose of such suits through summary procedure. We, therefore, pass an order for returning the plaint to the petitioner or his lawyer for presenting the same before the District Court.
